extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers, educators, public health and municipal officials
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of short local-news items and reports covering school programs, public health inspections, municipal improvements and equipment, safety campaigns, business transactions, and construction proposals. Each item summarizes events, procedures, or proposals relevant to city residents and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-district reading procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each school is requested to send one reader and one alternate reader to the inter-district reading assigned to his school. At these readings each child will be allowed three minutes for reading a familiar section supplied by his school. Sight reading will also be furnished and brief tests of silent reading will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule: inter-district readings begin April 25 and continue to June 1. Schools should designate readers and alternates and prepare familiar sections; plan for sight-reading and short silent-reading tests during the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading clinic diagnostic protocol (Dr. C. Truman Gray)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before testing the child the teacher gives all information about his vision, hearing, breathing and attention. The child is given several prose selections of increased difficulty, several bits of poetry of a similar gradation, and a bit of oratory; then a set of printed questions to which he writes answers, and printed stories which he reads and reproduces. A careful record of the child's time and his number of errors on each experiment is kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced instrumentation used: darkened room projection of printed selection, phonograph recording of performance, camera to take pictures of eye movements, chest instrument to record breathing, and a projecting-machine shutter device to measure span of attention (number of words recalled beyond the stopped word). Purpose: diagnose causes of poor reading and identify remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for school medical inspection (uniformity and thoroughness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no uniformity in their methods... The calls vary from five minutes to one and a half hours, and the number of children examined from one or two or none, to twenty or thirty per day." Local board suggests "a more definite method of examination be required of the visiting physicians."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms include inadequate and inconsistent examinations, insufficient follow-up, and incomplete coverage (e.g., in only 248 schools were any examinations for physical defects made, and in these schools not more than one-third of pupils were examined). Remedies discussed: establishment of a department of school hygiene, clearer examination methods, and better oversight by the Board of Education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library procedures to prevent disease spread from returned books
rubrics_metrics.description: "Daily lists of the homes in which contagious disease is found are furnished to the library, and books that are returned from such homes are fumigated in a large vault at the main library. When a health inspector visits a home in which there is contagious disease... the cards identifying [the books] are removed by the inspector and mailed to the library. When the patient recovers and the health department fumigates the house, the library books are also fumigated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine: cooperate with health department, fumigate books returned from known-contagion homes, remove identification cards until safe. Note: average circulating books are not fumigated; library officials express doubt that books commonly spread disease, but take extra precautions for known cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and curatorial considerations for indigenous ritual artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zuni have an unwritten law that no white man is to have any of the objects used in their ceremonies, and that any one parting with them is entitled to have his throat cut. Many of the sacred symbols in Dr. Kroeber's possession were acquired after much trouble and not a little risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection, transport, and exhibition of ritual objects involve ethical risks and cultural prohibitions; curators should document provenance, be sensitive to secret/ceremonial contexts, and prepare careful arrangement and interpretation (Dr. Kroeber to arrange the collection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing dangerous street construction and traffic hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic conditions are regarded as so dangerous at the corner of Tremont and School streets, on account of the laying of the high-pressure pipes, that the mayor had ordered the contractor to work night and day, with forces as large as practicable, until the work is finished. It will probably be necessary to close School street some time this week... large piles of dirt at each corner and wagons so placed that at times it was practically impossible for vehicular traffic to move at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When construction creates acute traffic hazards: perform personal inspections, accelerate work (night/day shifts), reconfigure or close streets if necessary, and manage contractor placement of materials to avoid obstructing traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance coordination for undergrounding utilities before paving
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspector Samuel L. Wheeler "will try to place before the public service associates the plans for his work a year or more in advance. Thus the companies will have a chance to get their wires underground before the streets are paved."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan utility relocations well in advance of paving; hold conferences between city supervisors, street-railway officials, and public-service corporations so track relays and conduit work precede pavement to avoid tearing up new pavement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications for emergency water-main gate-closing equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: A motor truck with a power appliance for quickly closing heavy gates reduces work formerly requiring four men and forty-five minutes to ten minutes by one man. The device consists of a universal wrench socket with a worm gear, enclosed in an aluminum housing, mounted on the running board, driven off the truck transmission; gears of chrome or nickel steel, ball bearings, universal joint, indicator or counter for revolutions, and a shear pin safety device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design requirements: rapid operation (single-operator, ~10 minutes), reliability under emergency calls, flexibility to position over gate nut, durable materials, indicators or counters to confirm valve position, and a safety shear pin to prevent damage if valve seats with force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade crossing safety signage and public campaign standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Enormous signs, 24x10 feet, electrically illuminated at night, in black and white letters readable several blocks away, with messages urging motorists to stop, look and listen (e.g., 'THIS SIGN MAY SAVE YOUR LIFE TODAY... When approaching a crossing please stop, look and listen.'). Also suggestion to paint gates black and white for visibility (European practice) rather than plain white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signage specifications: large size, nighttime illumination, high-contrast lettering, prominent placement across highways approaching crossings; campaign should include recurring 'life saving bulletins' with clear action steps (watch for flagman, listen for bell, blow horn, look both ways). Consider gate color/contrast improvements for long-distance visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standards for business mergers (news content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report includes deal size (about $400,000), assets acquired (docks, property, business), inventory on hand (e.g., 75,000 tons of coal), dock capacities and locations, loading capacity, office use after sale, assumption of unfilled contracts, employment impact, and effect on company's market (expected increase of 300,000 to 400,000 tons yearly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good merger reporting should state purchase price, what tangible assets and inventory transfer, capacity and logistical details, contractual obligations assumed, staffing consequences, agency/representation, and strategic effect on business volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and specifications for first-class commercial hotel construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed eleven-story hotel costing about $1,250,000: first floor to contain office, reading-room, large public dining-room and buffet; basement rathskeller and kitchens; second floor additional dining and banquet rooms; guest rooms above, eleventh story for sample-rooms for commercial travellers. The building will be fireproof in every particular, practically no wood except doors and windows, concrete floors, tile and marble in public rooms and corridors, tiling in bathrooms, carpets elsewhere, heated and ventilated in an approved manner, elevators and stairs centrally located; exterior of limestone and brick in French Renaissance style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for a first-class commercial hotel: fireproof construction, durable and high-quality finishes, proper HVAC, centrally located vertical circulation, mixed-use storefront frontage, service entrances, adequate sample/trade facilities, and long-term commercial leases for ground-floor retail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal bond issuance and disclosure practices
rubrics_metrics.description: City sold a $1,000,000 bond issue with breakdown by loan purpose and rates (municipal building loan $200,000 at 4%, high school $150,000 at 4.5%, Fulton-street loan $400,000 at 4.5%, etc.), sold at a premium bringing interest down to 4.30%. Bidders named, premium and comparative bids reported. Interest on municipal bonds is tax-exempt; interest collectible without certificates and individuals not required to report the income to the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure should include total issue, purchaser, bid prices/premiums, effective interest rate, loan purpose and amounts, maturities and coupon rates, and tax treatment; reporting supports market confidence and informs local investors of relative yields and tax advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial import-substitution sourcing and innovation (brush manufacturing example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When imported water-color brushes from Germany became unobtainable due to the war, local investigators found that the 'most tender, delicate, yet strong and soft hair in the world is to be found only in a cow's ear' and arranged supply from stockyards; manufacturers tested and produced brushes artists considered superior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In supply crises, survey domestic sources and local specialties for substitutes, test material properties with end-users (artists), and coordinate brokers/manufacturers to establish new supply chains and resume production.
